variations.name: Reforestation / afforestation tech (drone seeding, seed & nursery tech, native species)
variations.description: Companies that plant or re-establish forests faster and cheaper using drone/aerial seeding, industrialized native-seed banking and nurseries, and (in a few cases) biotech-enhanced trees, so degraded and burned land can be restored at the scale climate goals require.

companies.name: Mast Reforestation (DroneSeed)
companies.what: End-to-end post-wildfire reforestation: owns Silvaseed and Cal Forest nurseries plus DroneSeed aerial seeding, funded by selling verified carbon credits
companies.signal: $25M Series B Feb 2025 co-led by Social Capital and Pulse Fund; pivoting into biomass-burial (BiCRS) carbon removal

companies.name: Dendra Systems
companies.what: Oxford UK drone seeding carrying 50+ native species at once plus an AI ecology/monitoring platform for large-scale restoration
companies.signal: ~$15.7M raised; April 2025 World Bank partnership for Sahel RESILAND aerial reforestation

companies.name: Flash Forest
companies.what: Canadian drone seeding with pneumatic seed-pod launchers focused on wildfire burn zones
companies.signal: 2.9M+ trees across 52 projects; 2025 agreement with Chile to reforest Valparaiso and Maule

companies.name: Land Life Company
companies.what: Netherlands tech-driven reforestation using drones, AI monitoring and planting tech across degraded land worldwide
companies.signal: ~95 staff; 10M+ trees / 11,250 ha restored; ABN AMRO Clearing 5-yr program; ~$2M top-up Jan 2025

companies.name: Terraformation
companies.what: Hawaii-based native-seed banking at scale plus the open-source Terraware forest-management platform, enabling locally-led native reforestation
companies.signal: 139M seeds stored, 68 projects across 18 countries; cut ~half of staff in 2023 then repositioned to project finance and grants

companies.name: Living Carbon
companies.what: Plants biotech 'photosynthesis-enhanced' fast-growing poplars and reforests former mine lands in Appalachia for carbon credits
companies.signal: $36M+ raised (Temasek, Lowercarbon); Microsoft 1.4M-tonne deal (2025) and Octopus Energy $500M deal (2026); gene-trait efficacy still scientifically contested

companies.name: Morfo
companies.what: French restoration-tech company combining drone seeding of native species with ARR project development, Brazil-focused
companies.signal: Launched a call for ARR projects in Brazil (Feb 2025) to aggregate developer pipeline for carbon buyers

variations.white_space: Pure drone-seeding remains seed-efficiency- and survival-limited (DroneSeed's original credits 'failed to materialize', pushing Mast toward biomass burial), so the durable economics sit in seed/nursery supply and credit-funded full-service planting rather than the aircraft themselves.

variations.name: Restoration project developers & forest carbon project origination (ARR)
variations.description: Developers that originate, finance and operate afforestation/reforestation/revegetation (ARR) carbon-removal projects on degraded land, turning long-dated corporate offtakes into upfront capital for tree planting.

companies.name: Mombak
companies.what: Buys degraded Brazilian Amazon pasture and replants 100+ native species, selling durable carbon removals to hyperscalers
companies.signal: $30M USV-led Series A (Apr 2025), ~$200M raised since 2021; $150M+ removal offtakes with Google, Microsoft, Meta, McLaren; R$160M New Climate Fund deal

companies.name: re.green
companies.what: Large-scale Brazilian Atlantic Forest and Amazon ARR restoration developer
companies.signal: R$80M from BNDES plus R$100M more via BNDES/Santander Climate Fund in 2025

companies.name: Chestnut Carbon
companies.what: US-Southeast afforestation developer planting 35M+ native hardwood/softwood trees on ~60,000 acres for durable removals
companies.signal: $160M Series B (CPPIB-led, Feb 2025) plus $210M JPMorgan-led non-recourse facility (Jul 2025); two Microsoft offtakes (~7M and ~7.4M tonnes)

companies.name: Reforest'Action
companies.what: France-based developer/financier of certified (VCS, Gold Standard) reforestation and agroforestry projects funded by corporate buyers
companies.signal: Operates a global certified-project portfolio and corporate funding marketplace

companies.name: American Forests
companies.what: Century-old US conservation nonprofit running the Reforest America Carbon Program (RACP) to connect climate-smart reforestation to carbon finance
companies.signal: RACP active in 2025 to bridge high upfront cost / long tree-growth timelines for landowners

variations.white_space: Capital is now abundant for marquee Brazilian/US developers, but ARR still carries 30-60 year delivery risk and thin track records; the gap is bankable insurance/guarantee structures and standardized non-recourse project finance (Chestnut's JPMorgan facility is a first-of-kind) that let mid-size developers scale without dilutive equity.

variations.name: Forest / biomass carbon MRV (satellite, lidar, AI)
variations.description: Measurement, reporting and verification firms that use satellite imagery, airborne/terrestrial lidar and machine learning to estimate forest carbon stocks and change, replacing slow and expensive field plots and underpinning credit integrity.

companies.name: Pachama
companies.what: Satellite + lidar + AI MRV platform that verifies forest conservation and reforestation projects
companies.signal: ~$79M raised (Breakthrough, Amazon, Lowercarbon); ACQUIRED by Carbon Direct in Nov 2025 to bolster its MRV stack

companies.name: Chloris Geospatial
companies.what: Satellite-based measurement of forest carbon stock-change and ecosystem change for project and portfolio MRV
companies.signal: $8.5M Series A (Jul 2025) led by Future Energy Ventures, with AXA IM Alts, At One Ventures, Cisco Foundation

companies.name: CTrees
companies.what: Science nonprofit using AI + satellite + lidar to estimate carbon in every tree on Earth and run an open jurisdictional MRV (JMRV) tool
companies.signal: AWS Imagine Grant (2024); released open aboveground-biomass data 2000-2025; widely cited as reference layer

companies.name: Kanop
companies.what: Paris startup measuring forest carbon and ecosystem services from high-res satellite + AI for project developers
companies.signal: Early stage (~$1.15M raised); selected for the EU CASSINI space accelerator in 2025

companies.name: Space Intelligence
companies.what: Edinburgh firm producing high-accuracy global forest-cover and biomass maps (Habitat/Carbon mapping) for project MRV and nature monitoring
companies.signal: Series A (2024) led by AzurX Space Ventures with Intercontinental Exchange participating

variations.name: Deforestation & conversion monitoring (incl. EUDR compliance)
variations.description: Platforms that detect deforestation and land conversion via radar/optical satellite and turn it into supply-chain due-diligence, especially for EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) compliance where importers must prove goods are deforestation-free.

companies.name: Satelligence
companies.what: Netherlands radar+optical (Sentinel-1/2, Landsat) deforestation and land-use monitoring positioned as Europe's largest EUDR data provider
companies.signal: Grew from 3 to ~40 staff in 5 years; engaged in EU pilots; Fairtrade and Prewave partnerships

companies.name: osapiens
companies.what: Germany EUDR compliance SaaS automating due diligence, traceability, DDS generation and TRACES submission
companies.signal: Trusted by 700+ industry leaders for EUDR

companies.name: IntegrityNext
companies.what: Germany ESG/supplier platform with an EUDR module running supplier-data upload through DDS and direct TRACES submission
companies.signal: Large supplier ESG network targeting the Dec 2025 EUDR deadline

companies.name: Prewave
companies.what: Austria AI supply-chain risk platform automating supplier engagement and EUDR monitoring (built with Satelligence and Taylor Wessing)
companies.signal: ~€63M Series B (2024)

companies.name: Global Forest Watch (WRI)
companies.what: WRI-run open platform whose GLAD/RADD deforestation alerts are the free data backbone under many commercial EUDR tools
companies.signal: Foundational, free near-real-time alert layer used industry-wide

companies.name: Orbify
companies.what: No-code Earth-observation platform offering EUDR deforestation-monitoring and due-diligence SaaS
companies.signal: Featured in 2025 EUDR-SaaS roundups; early-stage geospatial player

variations.white_space: Demand is almost entirely regulation-driven, so repeated EUDR timeline slippage and political 'simplification' pressure (application now phased from Dec 2025 for large operators) is the key risk; vendors that diversify into voluntary deforestation-free sourcing and Scope-3 monitoring are less exposed than pure compliance plays.

variations.name: Supply-chain traceability & sourcing platforms
variations.description: Software that maps multi-tier agricultural supply chains down to plot/origin and attaches verifiable chain-of-custody and claims data, enabling deforestation-free sourcing for commodities like cocoa, coffee, palm, soy and timber.

companies.name: Sourcemap
companies.what: MIT-born platform mapping products to raw-material origin with transaction-level traceability and EUDR-grade due diligence
companies.signal: Used by large global brands (e.g. AG1); 2024 partnership with Provenance for end-to-end traceability

companies.name: Provenance
companies.what: UK platform producing verified product claims (regenerative, low-carbon, fair trade) backed by chain-of-custody evidence
companies.signal: Strong food/beauty adoption via retailer supplier-engagement programs; Sourcemap partnership

companies.name: TraceX
companies.what: India blockchain agri-supply-chain traceability connecting participants and supporting EUDR, ESPR, CSRD and DPP
companies.signal: Users include Rainforest Alliance and Organic India; listed on the FAO STI innovations portal

companies.name: Rainforest Alliance
companies.what: NGO certifier whose deforestation-free standard and farm/cooperative traceability underpin cocoa, coffee and tea sourcing
companies.signal: Global certification scheme integrating satellite partners (e.g. Satelligence) for risk assessment

companies.name: osapiens
companies.what: Also serves as a traceability layer, bundling multi-tier mapping with EUDR due-diligence and reporting in one platform
companies.signal: 700+ customers spanning compliance and traceability use cases

variations.white_space: The hard, unsolved layer is reliable first-mile/plot-level origin data from millions of smallholders who lack resources to collect and own it; affordable producer-side data capture (not just importer-side dashboards) is the opening, otherwise traceability stays approximate at the farm gate.

variations.name: Forest carbon credit ratings, registries & marketplaces
variations.description: The integrity-and-transactions layer: independent rating agencies that score credit quality, the standards/registries that issue and track credits, and marketplaces that let buyers procure them.

companies.name: Sylvera
companies.what: UK carbon-credit rating agency (AAA-D scale) combining satellite, lidar and project data, plus market analytics
companies.signal: ~$96M raised (Index Ventures, Balderton); publishes State of Carbon Credits

companies.name: BeZero Carbon
companies.what: UK rating agency scoring VCM credits (AAA-D) and expanding into CORSIA and Article 6 compliance markets
companies.signal: $32M Series C; ~$90M+ raised total

companies.name: Calyx Global
companies.what: US rating agency that moved to the AAA-D scale in Jan 2025 and absorbed the Renoster team to deepen forestry coverage
companies.signal: VC-backed; converged on market-standard methodology and scale in 2025

companies.name: Verra
companies.what: Runs the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), the world's largest credit registry and the dominant forestry/REDD+ standard
companies.signal: Largest issuer of credits; ARR methodology VM0047 v1.1 received ICVCM CCP approval Oct 2025

companies.name: Gold Standard
companies.what: WWF-founded Swiss non-profit standard and registry certifying high-integrity carbon and SDG-impact projects
companies.signal: One of the two leading global certification/registry bodies alongside Verra

companies.name: Patch
companies.what: API/enterprise carbon-procurement marketplace for buyers to access, evaluate and buy credits
companies.signal: ~$55M raised (a16z-led Series B); 2025 strategic partnership with Cloverly

companies.name: Cloverly
companies.what: Self-serve carbon marketplace and API for procuring and retiring credits, including forestry
companies.signal: Partnered with Patch in 2025 to streamline corporate buyer access

variations.name: Peatland & wetland conservation / restoration
variations.description: Protecting and rewetting carbon-dense peat swamp forests, mangroves and wetlands, whose disproportionate carbon stocks make them high-value but high-risk credit sources prone to reversal and tenure disputes.

companies.name: Permian Global
companies.what: UK developer managing tropical peatland REDD+, including the 149,800 ha Katingan Mentaya peat-swamp project in Central Kalimantan
companies.signal: Katingan averages ~7.5M VCUs/year; triple-gold VCS+CCB rated

companies.name: PT Rimba Makmur Utama (Katingan)
companies.what: Indonesian project owner/developer of the Katingan peatland conservation project (with Permian Global)
companies.signal: 41M+ Verra credits issued since 2013

companies.name: PT Rimba Raya Conservation
companies.what: Developer of the Rimba Raya peat-swamp REDD+ project, once the world's largest avoided-deforestation project
companies.signal: 33.6M credits issued, but Indonesia revoked its license Mar 2024; a Jakarta court voided the revocation Jul 2024 (under appeal), leaving CCB status in legal limbo

companies.name: Carbon Streaming Corp
companies.what: Carbon-credit streaming/financier that prepaid for Rimba Raya volumes and absorbed the fallout from its revocation
companies.signal: Issued multiple investor updates / write-down risk on Rimba Raya through 2024

companies.name: IUCN Peatland Carbon Code
companies.what: Standard for temperate/non-tropical degraded-peatland restoration (rewetting), opening a new credit class beyond the tropics
companies.signal: First ex-post credits expected to verify around June 2025; still nascent issuance

variations.white_space: Credible supply is concentrated in a handful of Indonesian mega-projects exposed to political tenure and reversal risk (Rimba Raya's license fight), while temperate-peat MRV (water-table and flux measurement) is immature; the opening is robust rewetting MRV plus aggregation of many small parcels into financeable temperate-peatland portfolios.

variations.name: Wildfire-resilience forest management & post-fire reforestation
variations.description: Technology to reduce wildfire risk to forests, the carbon they store and the grid that runs through them, plus replanting after fires, addressing wildfire as both a forest-loss and emissions driver.

companies.name: Vibrant Planet
companies.what: 'Land Tender' SaaS that fuses data to map wildfire risk and co-develop mitigation plans with land managers, utilities and tribes
companies.signal: Venture-backed (~$30M+); state contracts; early Tahoe Fund backing for Land Tender

companies.name: BurnBot
companies.what: Robotic prescribed-burn / mechanical fuel-treatment machines that clear hazardous fuel loads safely
companies.signal: $20M VC + $30M in fuel-treatment contracts; targeting ~15 machines and 3,000 acres treated by end of 2025

companies.name: Kodama Systems
companies.what: Retrofits forestry equipment for remote/autonomous thinning to cut fuel loads, and buries felled timber for durable carbon credits
companies.signal: $5.95M seed (Tahoe Fund and others); selling biomass-burial removals to Frontier/Stripe

companies.name: Mast Reforestation
companies.what: Restores severely burned forestland and buries unmerchantable fire-killed trees (BiCRS), selling removal credits to fund replanting
companies.signal: $25M Series B (2025); first Mast Wood Preserve biomass-burial project in central Montana (~900 acres post-fire)

companies.name: Overstory
companies.what: AI vegetation-intelligence from satellite imagery for wildfire prevention and grid/vegetation-management for utilities
companies.signal: $43M Series B (Nov 2025) led by Blume Equity with Energy Impact Partners

companies.name: Pano AI
companies.what: AI-powered mountaintop camera network for ultra-early wildfire detection and situational awareness
companies.signal: Series B (2024); deployments across western US and Australia, featured among LA-fire response startups

variations.white_space: The category splits into detection (Pano, Overstory), fuel treatment (BurnBot, Kodama) and post-fire replanting (Mast) with little integration; the gap is a single risk-to-remediation loop and, critically, durable revenue beyond episodic state/utility grants, since most fuel-treatment economics still lean on credits or public money.

variations.name: REDD+ avoided-deforestation & improved forest management (IFM) developers
variations.description: Developers that earn credits by keeping standing forests standing (REDD+) or improving harvest regimes on managed forests (IFM) — the single largest forestry credit category, and the one most damaged by over-crediting and baseline scandals.

companies.name: South Pole
companies.what: Once the world's largest carbon developer/trader; originated and marketed REDD+ at scale
companies.signal: Kariba REDD+ over-crediting scandal led it to terminate the contract (Oct 2023), overhaul leadership (new CEO May 2024) and restructure

companies.name: Wildlife Works
companies.what: Community-based REDD+ pioneer (e.g. the Kasigau Corridor, Kenya) tying avoided deforestation to local livelihoods
companies.signal: Long-running Verra-registered REDD+ portfolio; a defining template for the model

companies.name: Everland
companies.what: Marketing/distribution arm for REDD+ credits (including Wildlife Works projects) and a vocal defender of REDD+ integrity
companies.signal: Issued public rebuttals to 2023 REDD+ over-crediting criticism

companies.name: Permian Global
companies.what: Tropical forest + peat REDD+ developer (Katingan Mentaya) emphasizing high-integrity avoided-deforestation
companies.signal: Katingan ~7.5M VCUs/year, triple-gold rated

companies.name: Finite Carbon
companies.what: North America's leading forest carbon developer, mostly IFM projects on private and tribal land
companies.signal: 60+ projects since 2009; majority-owned by bp

companies.name: Anew Climate
companies.what: Large US carbon-project originator (formed from Bluesource + Element Markets) active in IFM and environmental commodities since 2001
companies.signal: One of the largest US offset suppliers/originators

companies.name: EFM (Ecotrust Forest Management)
companies.what: US forestland investment manager running improved-forest-management funds that generate carbon removals
companies.signal: Microsoft agreed to purchase ~3M IFM carbon-removal credits from EFM

variations.white_space: Although crowded and high-volume, avoided-deforestation baselines were systematically over-credited (Kariba, multiple Verra REDD+ projects), collapsing buyer trust and prices; the reset opportunity is jurisdictional REDD+ (ART/TREES) and re-issuance under Verra's consolidated allocated-baseline methodology (VM0048) with third-party ratings baked in, rather than project-by-project self-reported baselines.
